_comment: The Vana Personal Server's composed PDPP AS + RS. RUN AND VERIFIED.
The ref under test is the integration owner's composed tree, which carries
both PDPP halves. A resource-server-only ref is NOT a target on its own:
feat/pdpp-record-storage-rs deletes the authorization server outright, so
the consent journey this adapter drives cannot run and the report would be
skips rather than findings. scripts/vana-target.sh refuses such a ref.
Do not boot this by hand. scripts/vana-target.sh checks out the pinned ref,
installs, builds, boots, seeds every stream and its blobs, and tears the
whole thing down:
export PDPP_VANA_PS=/path/to/personal-server-ts
scripts/vana-target.sh up
eval "$(scripts/vana-target.sh env)"
npx tsx src/cli.ts --target targets/vana-personal-server.json
scripts/vana-target.sh stop
The ref is pinned in scripts/vana-target.sh and is the integration owner's
to change, not this suite's. When they publish a new commit, override it
rather than editing anything here:  PDPP_VANA_REF=<sha> vana-target.sh up
ownerBootstrapToken resolves from the PDPP_VANA_OWNER_TOKEN environment
variable at run time. The server mints a fresh dev token on every boot, so
no committed value can ever be correct -- and a real deployment's credential
committed by habit is a leak. scripts/vana-target.sh exports it for you.
operatorToken resolves from PDPP_VANA_OPERATOR_TOKEN the same way, and is
the credential for POST /pdpp/declarations -- the declaration acceptance
surface the nine AS-16 cases need. It is the OPERATOR's, never a client's:
a client able to submit its own declaration could declare itself authority
over any source. vana-target.sh configures it (PS_ACCESS_TOKEN) at boot and
exports it; without it the server does not mount the route and those cases
report skip naming the hook.
The declaration cases submit under a THIRD connector (conformance), for
which vana-target.sh seeds a scope row and nothing else -- no records, no
declared stream. That row is what lets this server's connector gate accept
the cases' positive controls at all; the two seeded streams the RS oracles
read are unchanged.
This deployment is CO-LOCATED (one origin) and uses a session-based journey
(authorize -> review -> approve -> PKCE code exchange) rather than the
reference's RFC 9126 PAR + consent route. Core pins neither: Section 6 defines
the selection request and Section 7 the resolved grant, not the route between
them. Both are conformant, and the case bodies never see the difference.
Two deployment facts that are configuration, not findings:
- /pdpp/v1/revoke takes form encoding, not JSON (as do /token and
/introspect); the consent endpoints take JSON.
- one owner is bound to the server, so there is no second subject. RS-12
reports skip naming that rather than passing on no evidence.
Declare ALL THREE streams below in the boot declaration and give each a
data_files scope row, then seed all three. The stream-membership oracles
(RS-2 enforcement, RS-6 error classification) work by holding one stream OUT
of the grant, so a single-stream deployment can only report skip on them.
Seed several records into top_artists as well: a stream too short to produce
a page cursor cannot exercise the cursor/changes_since token-space
separation case.
playlists is the third stream and exists for two clauses the other two
cannot reach between them. It declares NO consent_time_field -- Core makes
that absence the normative signal that a stream does not support time-range
filtering, so AS-2 (5.2-4, 6.8-2) and AS-11's v0.2 window case need a stream
that genuinely omits it, and a bogus field name would test 5.2-3 instead.
And its primaryKey names TWO columns, which is what RS-1's canonical
array-encoding clause acts on; a single-column key encodes as a bare string
and that clause never fires. top_artists and saved_tracks now state the
consentTimeField they have always declared in the boot declaration: without
it the suite believed no stream was time-range-capable and AS-2 skipped for
want of a positive control.
Run: tsx src/cli.ts --target targets/vana-personal-server.json
streams[].expectedOwnerMetadata is RS-14's oracle input: the schema field
types come from scripts/vana-target.sh's boot declaration (the authoritative
source), never from this server's own metadata endpoint. That declaration
declares no query.range_filters, views, or relationships for either stream,
so query/views/relationships are left absent here rather than invented --
RS-14 then checks schema completeness/content only, which is what this
deployment actually declares.
blobFixture names a blob vana-target.sh really uploaded through POST
/v1/blobs/ingest and referenced from the seeded media record, so RS-1's
byte-fetch case has a blob to fetch through an authorized record. The ids
and digest arrive as ${ENV_VAR} placeholders because the server mints ids at
upload time -- no committed value could be right. sha256/sizeBytes are what
the SEEDER computed from the bytes it sent, never read back from the target:
an expectation sourced from the server under test could not fail.
outOfGrantBlobId is a SECOND blob that really exists and that no record in
the granted stream references -- the negative case needs it, because a 404
on a fabricated id proves nothing about a server that 404s everything.
singleUseGrants is true because this server supports single_use grants.
AS-10/single-use-grant-consumed will still report skip against this
adapter: the case needs a reissueAgainstConsumedGrant hook to attempt a
second token issuance against the SAME consumed grant id, and this
adapter implements no such hook yet. That is a harness-coverage gap, not
an unsupported target feature -- do not read the skip as a capability
claim walked back.
expiryFixture registers a SECOND, dedicated client (expiring_widget) with
an operator-configured pdpp.clients[].grantLifetimeSeconds, so AS-8's
expired-grant oracle exercises this deployment's real operator policy
rather than a fabricated token. music_recommendations above is untouched
and keeps its ordinary, non-expiring grant -- the pagination/refresh cases
that expect a grant to stay usable partway through a run are unaffected.
grantLifetimeSeconds here MUST match the value vana-target.sh registers
for expiring_widget at boot. expectedRecord is a subset of the seeded
media record (vana-target.sh seed_blobs, med_1) the pre-expiry positive
control must find before the oracle trusts the token -- a 200 with no
matching record throws rather than skipping.
It reads the media stream, not top_artists, and the `stream` key above is
what says so. This control pins an EXACT record, and RS-7's projection
cases rewrite a field of the first live record on the first mutable_state
stream's sync page -- a top_artists record. Whichever ran first decided
whether AS-8 passed. media is written once at seed time and by nothing
else, so the ordering dependency is gone rather than hidden behind a
looser match.
